title: Microsoft, Meta, and AWS ship AI Services revenue breakouts by fiscal Q3 2026
body: By the fiscal Q3 2026 print cycle Microsoft, Meta, and AWS each carve out a discrete AI Services revenue line in a 10-Q footnote, following the Alphabet-led Q4 2026 cadence that the sell-side preview cohort has now hardened around. The Tuesday catalysts trace a tightening run-up to the May 21 Alphabet analyst day, now at T-minus-two calendar days. A Tuesday 247 Wall St positioning note reports Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies, and Goldman Sachs Equity Research nudging the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 89 percent — a one-point uptick from Monday's 88 percent — with the cohort citing the unchanged Friday SEC Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter as the settled disclosure-precedent input. A Tuesday VentureBeat aggregation reiterates the cohort's consensus that Microsoft, Meta, and AWS follow with their own AI Services revenue breakouts in their fiscal Q3 2026 prints, with the Alphabet-led Q4 2026 print cadence unchanged. The capital-markets backdrop that the disclosure shift will price into is hardening on the same Tuesday tape: Cerebras CBRS holds the Friday $198.60 close as its reference anchor with the five-desk analyst spread bracketing the stock inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging to about 38 percent of float, and the May 21 analyst day treated by desks as the first session in the run-up where directional positioning typically firms ahead of a Mag-7 print catalyst. The Tuesday HPCwire AIwire note further reports Tenstorrent's SEC Corp Fin first-round comment-letter response at its twelve-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval ahead of a likely second-round letter, holding an early-August public-filing target, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster steady at six with confidential-submission filing target unchanged at the final week of June — a three-name AI-accelerator IPO pipeline that gives equity analysts a fresh public comparable set against which a hyperscaler AI Services line item is the missing disclosure piece. The structural force is that once one hyperscaler — Alphabet — ships a discrete AI Services footnote against a settled Corp Fin sample comment letter, peer 10-Q disclosure consistency under Reg S-K item 303 plus sell-side modeling demand plus a public AI-accelerator comparable set leaves Microsoft, Meta, and AWS with no defensible reason to keep AI Services bundled inside aggregate Intelligent Cloud, Family of Apps, or AWS segment revenue through another quarter. The most likely landing is Microsoft, Meta, and AWS each disclosing a discrete AI Services revenue line in their fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q filings, each citing the Alphabet precedent and the SEC Corp Fin sample comment letter as the disclosure-precedent input, with the sell-side cohort retiring the Alphabet-versus-peers asymmetry from its modeling notes. Bear case is that one of the three opts for a wider AI plus emerging-products bucket rather than a pure AI Services line, deferring the clean breakout into fiscal Q4 2026; absent that, the three-name cohort prints the breakout inside fiscal Q3 2026.

reasoning.because: Sell-side cohort nudges Alphabet AI Services 10-Q breakout probability to 89 percent.
reasoning.given: Cohort consensus that Microsoft, Meta, and AWS follow in fiscal Q3 2026 prints holds unchanged.
reasoning.so_that: Microsoft, Meta, and AWS each disclose a discrete AI Services revenue line in their 10-Q footnotes.
reasoning.landing: By fiscal Q3 2026; Microsoft, Meta, AWS each ship the breakout.
reasoning.plain_language: Big tech rivals will soon have to spell out exactly how much money their AI products earn, instead of hiding it inside bigger numbers.

summary: Tuesday sell-side notes nudge Alphabet's AI Services 10-Q breakout probability to 89 percent into the May 21 analyst day, with cohort consensus that Microsoft, Meta, and AWS follow in fiscal Q3 2026. By fiscal Q3 2026 the three each ship a discrete AI Services line.
